title: Closed affine relation presentations on open pieces of a separated locally quasi-finite space
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $T$ an $S$-scheme, $E$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and $f:E\to T$ a morphism. Assume that for every representable etale scheme chart $h_V\to E$, the composite $V\to T$ is locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite], and that $\Delta_{E/T}:E\to E\times_TE$ is a closed immersion on all scheme tests [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-closed-immersion]. There is a set-indexed covering of $E$ by open subspaces $X_i$ [def-a1-space-open-subspace], affine opens $T_i\subseteq T$, and affine schemes $U_i,R_i$ over $T_i$, with the following properties. The map $X_i\to T$ factors through $T_i$; every representable etale scheme chart of $X_i$ is locally quasi-finite over $T_i$, and $\Delta_{X_i/T_i}$ is a closed immersion on all scheme tests. There is a representable surjective etale atlas $h_{U_i}\to X_i$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], $U_i\to T_i$ is locally quasi-finite, and $R_i=U_i\times_{X_i}U_i$ has surjective etale projections $s_i,t_i:R_i\to U_i$. The map $(s_i,t_i):R_i\to U_i\times_{T_i}U_i$ is a closed immersion and identifies $R_i(H)$ with an equivalence relation on $U_i(H)$ for every $T_i$-scheme $H$. The fppf sheaf quotient $U_i/R_i$ is canonically isomorphic to $X_i$, compatibly with its atlas and structure morphism; here the quotient is the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] on the big fppf site [def-pc-fppf-site] of $H\mapsto U_i(H)/R_i(H)$. For every $T_i$-scheme $B$, the atlas $U_i\times_{T_i}B\to X_i\times_{T_i}B$ has kernel pair $R_i\times_{T_i}B$ and its fppf sheaf quotient is canonically $X_i\times_{T_i}B$. Covering means that for every $S$-scheme $H$ and section $h_H\to E$, the open subschemes representing $h_H\times_EX_i$ cover $H$.

proof.text: Cover T by all affine opens [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. For each W form the sheaf pullback of E to W. Apply [lem-a1-space-separated-lqf-permanence], whose first conclusion supplies its algebraic-space structure. Apply [lem-a1-space-affine-atlas-open-cover] to this space. Paste the representing open squares to get open inclusions into E. An open inclusion is monic: test against a section and use monicity of the representing scheme open immersion. Identify each inclusion with its range subfunctor, giving the displayed OpenSubspace and isomorphism. The open-restriction clause of permanence gives exactly the relative chartwise quasi-finiteness and closed diagonal. Yoneda constructs uT from p followed by q.

proof.text: The composite family is jointly surjective on field-valued representatives. A field-valued representative maps into an affine neighbourhood of its unique scheme point in T; lift it to the sheaf pullback, then use the point-covering clause of the affine-atlas cover. For an arbitrary H and a section, represent each inverse image by an open immersion and identify it with its open range. A residue-field representative at any point lifts to a covering member after field extension. The cartesian square then factors that extended residue-field map through the inverse-image open. Its image in H is the original point, so that point belongs to the open. Thus the supremum of the opens is top, also for empty H.

source.place: Tag 03XX (proposition-locally-quasi-finite-separated-over-scheme), first three proof paragraphs: affine-base reduction, affine atlas and closed affine kernel pair; quotient identification after scheme base change.

proof.text: Test the representable etale atlas p against itself to construct R, s and t. Uniqueness of representing pullback squares transfers the etale and surjective properties of the test projections to both projections. On every scheme test, the pullback universal property gives unique relation witnesses precisely for pairs with equal p-image; equality supplies the equivalence relation. The atlas is fppf locally surjective, since its representing etale surjective scheme test is a singleton fppf covering. Factor p through its presheaf range. That epimorphism has the supplied relation as kernel pair, so Mathlib IsKernelPair.toCoequalizer gives the range coequalizer. Local surjectivity says the subsheaf closure of the range is the whole target. The subsheaf closure universal property therefore extends every equalizing map uniquely to the target. Descending p along the presheaf coequalizer gives eta and precisely the required hom-set bijections. This uses no global small-valued sheafification instance.

source.place: Tag 03XX (proposition-locally-quasi-finite-separated-over-scheme), first three proof paragraphs: affine-base reduction, affine atlas and closed affine kernel pair; quotient identification after scheme base change.

proof.text: Test the relative closed diagonal against h_(U times_Ti U), with the two maps induced by p. The resulting closed scheme R-prime is a second representative of the kernel pair: on sections its diagonal square describes exactly equal p-images, and pairs with equal p-image have equal Ti-image. Uniqueness gives R isomorphic to R-prime and identifies its map to the scheme product with the tested closed immersion. Transfer closedness along this isomorphism. The scheme product is affine [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], and a closed immersion has affine source over an affine target [def-weil-closed-immersion].

source.place: Tag 03XX (proposition-locally-quasi-finite-separated-over-scheme), first three proof paragraphs: affine-base reduction, affine atlas and closed affine kernel pair; quotient identification after scheme base change.

proof.text: For arbitrary B over Ti, form UB=U times_Ti B and RB=R times_Ti B in Over S. Representable scheme sheaves are algebraic spaces: their diagonals are represented by equalizers and their identity maps are etale surjective atlases. Thus [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] supplies XB=X times_Ti B. The two scheme pullback projections induce pB by the XB universal property. Pullback cancellation identifies pB as the base change of p, so its representable etaleness and surjectivity follow directly by pasting their scheme tests. Define sB,tB by their specified projections. The universal properties identify RB with the kernel pair of pB: a compatible pair gives an R-coordinate by the original kernel-pair property and a common B-coordinate. Uniqueness follows by the RB and UB pullback properties. Apply the range-and-subsheaf-closure quotient argument of step 3 to pB and its kernel pair. All witnesses and projection equations are retained.
